assigned.title: A resumed pass may not infer absence: fix what `complete` means
assigned.acceptance: `complete` means THE WHOLE SOURCE WAS OBSERVED, sufficient to infer absence -- not merely that this invocation reached end-of-enumeration. THE HAZARD, stated exactly. `IngestionPassResult.complete` is set when the provider's cursor runs out. A pass started from a non-null `resumeCursor` can reach that end having DELIBERATELY SKIPPED every page before the cursor, and it reports `complete: true`. `reconcileTombstones` takes `complete` as licence to infer absence, so every known content id living on a skipped page is unseen, is inferred withdrawn, and is mass-tombstoned. Under PL-0309's tombstone rule a tombstone is released only by a later complete pass that accepts the work again, so the damage is not self-healing on the next pass. WHY THIS IS NOT LIVE TODAY, and why that is not a reason to defer it: PL-0309's `schedule.ts` always passes `resumeCursor: null`, which keeps the hazard unreachable at the cost of re-reading the prefix every pass. The reviewer ruled it non-blocking for PL-0309 on exactly that ground and required this task BEFORE resume support is enabled. So the ordering constraint is the deliverable as much as the fix is: whoever adds resume must find this already closed. REQUIRED: absence inference is gated on a fact that a resumed pass cannot satisfy by accident. The implementer chooses the mechanism and states why -- a distinct field separating 'enumeration ended' from 'whole source observed', a fourth `TombstoneWithholdReason` for a resumed pass, or a `seenContentIds` set that makes the reconciliation exact rather than inferential. What is NOT acceptable is a comment telling a future caller not to resume, which is the state this task exists to replace. REQUIRED: a regression that fails against today's code. Start a pass from a `resumeCursor` positioned past a known id, let it run to the provider's end, and assert that id is NOT tombstoned. That test goes red on the current tree -- verify it does and say so -- which makes this a genuine red-to-green rather than a restatement. CONSIDER AND RULE ON, rather than silently skipping: `IngestionPassResult` publishes no seen set, and refusals carry native ids rather than derived content ids, so PL-0309 could not distinguish 'the complete pass saw this work and refused it' from 'never saw it' and took the conservative reading. If `seenContentIds` is the mechanism chosen here, say what it does to that narrowing. NOT IN SCOPE: enabling resume, backfill, or paging beyond `maxPages`; changing the tombstone-RELEASE rule PL-0309 delivered and the reviewer accepted; and redesigning `CatalogStore`, `applyPassToSnapshot` or `refreshCatalogIfDue`.
assigned.notes: Created 2026-09-22 on gpt-architect's FOLLOW-UP FINDING in the PL-0309 CHANGES_REQUESTED at 9dc9bc8, which ordered a separate task rather than a fix inside PL-0309. FOUND BY THE PL-0309 IMPLEMENTER IN A FILE ON ITS OWN SURFACE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED THERE: ingest.ts was writable to it, and it reported the hazard instead, on the ground that the fix changes what `complete` means or adds a fourth TombstoneWithholdReason -- a change to the rule that file's header is built around, and not something to fold into a task about scheduling. The reviewer agreed and ordered it separately. rights-review is on the gate list because a wrongly tombstoned work is a catalog that silently loses licensed content, and the release rule means it stays lost until a complete pass re-accepts it.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; lint --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; build --force, exit 0, 11 of 11. THREE SEPARATE INVOCATIONS, which is the procedure change this project adopted after the .next/types typecheck-build race was found in round 64 and which the reviewer then folded into PL-AI-0002's CI scope. The race is not fixed -- neither turbo.json nor apps/web/tsconfig.json is on PL-0313's surface -- so running them separately is the only thing available here, and it removes the race from this evidence without removing it from CI. THE CHANGE IS ONE TERNARY BRANCH AND A UNION MEMBER. TombstoneWithholdReason gains resumed_pass; the withheld computation gains options.resumeCursor !== null between incremental_pass and page_limit_reached; complete is derived from withheld and therefore needed no separate edit. No new field was added to IngestionPassResult, no signature changed, and the type flows to every consumer through the existing barrel export, so tsc is what proves the four consumers of complete and tombstonesWithheld still agree.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2723 passed 1 skipped against the 2719/1 baseline: +4, exactly the four tests added to ingest.test.ts, and the sum was recomputed from the per-package figures (100+67+68+47+208+252+373+260+288+152+908 = 2723). catalog-ingestion 148 to 152. test:scripts 0, repo:validate 0. THIS IS A GENUINE RED-TO-GREEN AND THE RED WAS OBSERVED ON THE UNMODIFIED TREE BEFORE THE FIX WAS WRITTEN, which the acceptance required rather than suggested: three of the four failed against cd6f3ef -- 'withholds tombstones when it started from a cursor, even reaching the end', 'still reports the enumeration ended, because that is a different fact', and 'names the resume rather than the page limit when both apply'. 3 failed, 17 passed. THE FOURTH TEST IS A CONTROL AND IT PASSED BEFORE THE FIX AS WELL AS AFTER: 'leaves an unresumed full pass able to infer absence, which is the point of the rule' asserts that a pass from the beginning that reaches the end still tombstones a known id it did not see. Without it a guard that simply withheld tombstones always would satisfy the other three, which would close the hazard by disabling the feature. AN HONEST NOTE ON THE FIRST RUN: all FOUR failed initially, because the page fixtures omitted the ok: true discriminant that ProviderPageResult requires and every existing test in the file supplies. The control test failing is what exposed it -- a regression suite where the control also goes red is measuring the harness, not the code -- so the fixtures were corrected and the red re-observed at three before a line of ingest.ts was touched. THE MECHANISM, and why not the alternatives: nextCursor === null already publishes 'the enumeration ended', so a second boolean field would need a rule about which one a caller believes. What was missing is not a fact about the cursor but whether this pass is a basis for inferring absence, which is exactly what tombstonesWithheld already answers for a failed, incremental or truncated pass. A resumed pass is a fourth member of that set. ORDERING IS REPORTING PRECEDENCE AND IS TESTED: a resumed pass that also ran out of page budget reports resumed_pass rather than page_limit_reached, because the prefix was skipped by choice and raising maxPages would not fix it. SEEN-CONTENT-IDS WAS CONSIDERED AND RULED AGAINST, which the acceptance asked for explicitly. ingest.ts already tracks seen-but-refused ids internally and already spares them from a tombstone, so that half was never broken. Publishing the set would matter only to the STORE, which today releases a tombstone when a complete pass ACCEPTS a work and could then release when a complete pass merely SAW it -- a change to the tombstone-release rule the reviewer accepted in PL-0309 and explicitly out of this task's scope. Shipping an unread field to enable a rule change nobody has approved is the wrong order; the argument a later task should answer is written into docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md rather than left in a commit message. WHAT THIS DOES NOT TURN ON: resume and backfill remain off, schedule.ts still passes resumeCursor null, and LIBERTY_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES still bounds the catalog a reader sees. What changed is that enabling resume is now a scheduling decision rather than a mass-deletion risk.

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests
